meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'butterfly (slang: call girl)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты зачем эту бабочку ночную привёл?
examples.trans: Why did you bring this lady of the night here?

examples.text: Я в Москве всех приличных бабочек знаю.
examples.trans: I know all the respectable call girls in Moscow.

meanings.note: слава богу = thank God (literally 'glory to God')

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's warm at last! Thank goodness. Now I'll make some tea too.

meanings.note: Comparative of много. Core Russian adv meaning 'more' in everyday speech.
Comparative of большой. Core Russian adv meaning 'more' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

Outdoor environment. Common masculine noun meaning 'air; outdoors' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Успокойся, пойдём на свежий воздух сейчас.
examples.trans: Calm down, let us go outside into fresh air now.

examples.text: Я просто стою и дышу воздухом.
examples.trans: I am just standing and breathing air.

meanings.note: With numbers: всего восемь лет. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: They will give only eight years.

examples.text: Предлагаю чистосердечное признание. Дадут всего восемь лет.

meanings.note: In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to breathe'.

examples.text: Лёша, что случилось? Дыши, сынок, дыши!
examples.trans: Lyosha, what happened? Breathe, son, breathe!

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: affectionate hypocoristic form of мама

examples.trans: Mommy, I love you very much!
Alright, mommy. I will lie down quickly.

meanings.note: in 'рабочее место' = workplace, job
На его место = in his place. Common neuter noun meaning 'place; seat' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Уже месяц = for a month now. Common masculine noun meaning 'month' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I've been living here for a month.
The election is in a month.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

нельзя.gloss: it is not allowed; one can't

meanings.note: The opposite of можно. Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'льзя').
Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'льзя').

examples.trans: Not allowed? All right, I'll go and do my homework.

нервничать.gloss: to be nervous, get worked up

meanings.en: to be nervous, worry, get worked up
meanings.note: Intransitive. Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'рвничать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be nervous, get worked up'.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, вам нельзя нервничать сейчас.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, you mustn't get worked up right now.
I am not getting worked up!

examples.text: Я не нервничаю! Рейтинг Самсонова сравнялся с нашим?
examples.trans: I'm not getting worked up! Has Samsonov's rating drawn level with ours?

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'almost, nearly' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Наш с вами город очень старый. Почти четыре века здесь были набеги.
examples.trans: Our town is very old. For almost four centuries there were raids here.

meanings.note: + genitive plural: пять рублей. Core Russian num meaning 'five' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же только начинаем. Через месяц будет пять тысяч.
examples.trans: But we're only just starting. In a month there'll be five thousand.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

examples.trans: You need to lure him onto your territory. Right where you are strong.

meanings.note: имей совесть! = have a heart! / shame on you!

meanings.note: + instrumental: стал сентиментальным
+ infinitive. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to become', paired with 'становиться'.

examples.trans: You've become too sentimental. And a leader has to be tough.
